content:
This clash feels a bit too similar to https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/1371637e68d6d4e6eebd3286c57c4b63e1b71f. I get that the output is different, but the concept is identical.

While waiting for other reviewers to chime in, please fix the following formatting issues:

- Please format "NONE" (in the Output section) as {{NONE}}.

- Please format "n" and "h" (in the Constraints section) as [[n]] and [[h]].

- Please use suitable ranges for n and h that closely match your test cases. Alternatively, please create more tests/validators that have more heights (greater n), and/or more varied height values (inclusive of negative values, though I'm not sure how that works).

- Please change the second line of the stub generator input to: loopline n h:int
I guess I will think of something else then. It seems very similar to the other one. Thank you

Just in case you decide to keep this contribution, below are a few points to follow up. Otherwise, please consider them as a reference for your future contributions:

Goal
* Please change "numbers"/"number" to "integers"/"integer".

* Please change "print" to "output".

Input
* Line 2: Please change "numbers" to "integers representing the heights of a mountain range".

Output
* Please change "Print all" to "<<Line 1:>> All".

Cases
* Test 3: Please change the input to use 3-digit integers for all [[h]].

* Please add Test 5 and Validator 5, where the input is a strictly decreasing sequence consisting of 1-digit, 2-digit and 3-digit integers.

Thanks.
You could add something to process, like give values in either meters or feet, so f.e. Mt. Everest is given as either 	8,848.86 m  or 29,031.7 ft.
